map.Lessons 7-4, 7-5 & 7-6 — part of the Bel: Lessons 7-4, 7-5 & 7-6. Part of the Below Zero arc. four quadrants · distance · polygons · 6.NOS.C.6/8 · 6.GR.A.3. Read it all the way. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It does not stop you.
map.Episode 3. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 3. Same crew. Same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you are set.
map.Ada's map cuts the city into four quadra: Ada's map cuts the city into four quadrants. Start at the upper right. Go counterclockwise: I, II, III, IV.
map.Every station is an ordered pair (x, y):: Each station is an ordered pair (x, y). East–west goes first. Then north–south. (2, 5) is NOT (5, 2).
map.Two relays must light next: (−3, 2) and: Two relays must light next: (−3, 2) and (4, −1). But the blackout mixed up my map. Five dots blink. Just two are real.
map.An ordered pair (x, y) locates a point:: An ordered pair (x, y) finds a point. x is first (left–right). Then y (up–down).
map.Read the pairs carefully, reader. Light: Read the pairs with care, reader. Light the wrong relay and we waste our power.
map.Five dots flicker on Ada's map, but only: Five dots blink on Ada's map. Just the relays at (−3, 2) and (4, −1) are real. Tap to light exactly those two. Tap again to turn one off. Then name their quadrants.
map.Conceptual: an ordered pair is (x, y). T: Conceptual: an ordered pair is (x, y). Start at the origin. The first number goes left (negative) or right (positive). The second goes down (negative) or up (positive).
map.Procedural: walk each pair: for (−1, 4): Procedural: walk each pair. For (−1, 4), go 1 block left. Then go 4 blocks up. Quadrants go counterclockwise from the upper right: I, then II, then III, then IV.
map.Cable time. Even elevation runs below ze: Cable time. Down here, the ground is below zero too. The old platform is at −6 meters.
map.And cable doesn't stretch. We count exac: And cable does not stretch. We count the exact blocks. No guessing.
map.Two runs tonight: across Fourth Street f: Two runs tonight. Across Fourth Street, from (−3, 4) to (5, 4). Down Second Avenue, from (2, −1) to (2, −6).
map.When two points share a coordinate, the: Two points can share a coordinate. Then the path between them is straight. Measure it with absolute values.
map.Measure both cable runs in blocks. Cable: Measure both cable runs in blocks. Cable A: (−3, 4) to (5, 4). Cable B: (2, −1) to (2, −6). Count with care. Priya cuts just once.
map.Conceptual: when two points share a coor: Conceptual: the two points share a coordinate. So the cable runs straight. Look at the numbers that change. Are they on OPPOSITE sides of zero? ADD their absolute values. Same side of zero? SUBTRACT them.
map.Procedural: like (−4, 1) to (2, 1): x cr: Procedural: take (−4, 1) to (2, 1). x crosses zero, so |−4| + |2| = 6 blocks. Take (7, −2) to (7, −9). Same side, so 9 − 2 = 7 blocks.
map.Midnight. One move left: ring the engine: Midnight. One move left. Ring the engine's part of town with cable. Then the whole grid lights up.
map.The Light Ring: a rectangle of cable thr: The Light Ring is a rectangle of cable. It goes through four corner relays. I sense its shape. You must measure it.
map.Width, height, then total cable. Three l: Width, height, then all the cable. Three locks, one ring. Reader, get us home.
map.Boss Gate: distances on the plane, plus: Boss Gate: find distances on the plane. Then find the perimeter of a grid polygon.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The city is watc: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The city is watching. (The city is cold, too.)
map.The ring's corner relays: (−4, −2), (3,: The ring's corner relays: (−4, −2), (3, −2), (3, 3), (−4, 3). Open all three locks to close the ring:
map.Total cable to close the ring (perimeter: All the cable to close the ring (perimeter):
map.Conceptual: a side's length is the dista: Conceptual: look at the coordinates that CHANGE. A side's length is the distance between them. Are they on opposite sides of zero? Then add the two distances. The perimeter is the trip around all four sides.
map.Procedural: a side from x = −2 to x = 6: Procedural: a side from x = −2 to x = 6 crosses zero. So 2 + 6 = 8 blocks. Perimeter short cut: 2 × (width + height).
map.Quadrant by quadrant — look at it glow!: Quadrant by quadrant. Look at it glow!
Twenty-four blocks of cable. Not one extra. We led, counted, and checked.
map.Achievement unlocked: city un-frozen. Ho: The city is warm again! Hot cocoa race starts now.
map.New distortion below city hall. A door s: A new distortion! It is under city hall. Its door is like a balance scale. It wants things EQUAL. To be continued…
map.The full story — Below Zero — is glowing: The full story is Below Zero. It waits at the gate. — A.V.

map.x = −2 → walk two blocks LEFT. y = −5 →: x = −2 → walk two blocks LEFT. y = −5 → walk five blocks DOWN.
map.Left and down lands in Quadrant III — th: Left and down is Quadrant III. There, both signs are negative.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.A point has positive x and negative y. W: A point has positive x and negative y. Which quadrant is it in, 1–4?
map.Measure (−6, 3) to (3, 3): the y-values: Measure (−6, 3) to (3, 3). The y-values match. So the run goes side to side.
map.x goes from −6 to 3 — opposite sides of: x goes from −6 to 3. Those are opposite sides of zero. So add the distances: |−6| + |3| = 9 blocks.
map.Now (4, −1) to (4, −7): both y-values ar: Now (4, −1) to (4, −7). Both y-values are below zero. Same side. So subtract: 7 − 1 = 6 blocks.
map.Width: x runs from −1 to 3, crossing zer: Width: x goes from −1 to 3. It crosses zero → 1 + 3 = 4. Height: y goes from −2 to 1 → 2 + 1 = 3.
map.A grid rectangle is 6 wide and 3 tall. H: A grid rectangle is 6 wide and 3 tall. How much cable goes around it?
map.Check the signs: in (−3, 2), the −3 mean: Check the signs. In (−3, 2), the −3 means 3 blocks LEFT of the engine. Not right.
map.The second number is the up–down move: (: The second number is the up–down move. (−3, 2) goes UP 2. It does not go down.
map.Re-walk each pair from the origin: left–: Walk each pair again from the origin. Left–right first. Then up–down.
map.Relays lit! Now the quadrants — count co: Relays lit! Now the quadrants. Go counterclockwise from the upper right: I, II, III, IV.
map.(−3, 2) glows in Quadrant II and (4, −1): (−3, 2) glows in Quadrant II. (4, −1) glows in Quadrant IV. The relays link across the city!
map.Cable A crosses x = 0 — don't subtract s: Cable A crosses x = 0. Do not subtract across zero. Add each end's distance from the y-axis.
map.Cable A runs sideways: only the x-number: Cable A runs side to side. Just the x-numbers change. Count the blocks between them.
map.Both y-values sit on the SAME side of ze: Both y-values: SAME side of zero. Subtract the smaller distance from the bigger one.
map.Cable B runs up–down: only the y-numbers: Cable B runs up–down. Just the y-numbers change. Count with care below zero.
map.8 blocks across, 5 blocks down — both ca: 8 blocks across, 5 blocks down. Both cables fit just right!
map.Lock 1 holds. Width: x runs from −4 to 3: Lock 1 holds. Width: x goes from −4 to 3. Those are opposite sides of zero. So ADD each end's distance from the y-axis.
map.Lock 2 holds. Height: y runs from −2 up: Lock 2 holds. Height: y goes from −2 up to 3. Opposite sides again. Add the distances.
map.Lock 3 holds. 35 is the AREA inside the: Lock 3 holds. 35 is the AREA inside the ring. The cable goes around the EDGE. Add all four sides.
map.Lock 3 holds. That's one width plus one: Lock 3 holds. That is one width plus one height. The ring needs BOTH widths and BOTH heights.
map.Lock 3 holds. Perimeter is the whole tri: Lock 3 holds. Perimeter is the whole trip around: width + height + width + height.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 24 blocks of cable close: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 24 blocks of cable close the ring. The Light Ring blazes! Axiom City lights up, quadrant by quadrant!
Yes! Now go back and open that gate.
